name: create_alert_rule
title: Create Alert Rule
description:
Create a Sentry Alert (workflow) that sends notifications, such as Slack, email or PagerDuty, when its issue or monitor sources trigger.
Use get_alert_options for available actions, integrations, conditions, and sources. All notification providers use their native config and data fields.
To copy an Alert, read get_alert_rule(kind='issue') and pass its configuration here; component IDs are discarded while integration and destination IDs are retained. New trigger groups require logicType='any-short'.
To reuse an existing Alert across projects, use update_alert_rule instead.
Supply projectSlugs for project issue streams and/or detectorIds for individual monitors. Pass detectorIds=[] explicitly to create an Alert without sources; it will not send notifications until connected.
New Alerts default to active with a 30-minute notification interval. Use status='disabled' to configure one before enabling it.
Project-constrained sessions require sources exclusively within that project. All-project sources require Sentry's feature and org:write in addition to alerts:write.
After a timeout or error, search for the Alert before retrying: creation may already have succeeded.
<examples>
create_alert_rule(organizationSlug='my-org', name='Backend notifications', status='disabled', detectorIds=[], actionFilters=[])
</examples>

name: create_metric_monitor
title: Create Metric Monitor
description:
Create a Sentry Metric Monitor that detects when a metric, such as an error count or latency, crosses a threshold. Supports Static, Percent or Dynamic detection.
Provide the complete query, detection config and conditions. Time windows and comparison deltas use seconds. Percent comparisons are absolute: 110 means 10% higher.
To copy a monitor, use the query, config and conditionGroup from get_metric_monitor_details. Component IDs are discarded; new condition groups use logicType='any'.
New monitors start ACTIVE and immediately evaluate data. Initially disabled creation is not supported. Use update_metric_monitor to disable an existing monitor.
workflowIds optionally connect existing notification Alerts, including shared Alerts, without modifying their configuration. Create an Alert separately with create_alert_rule if needed.
Dataset access, quota, aggregate, window and historical-data requirements are enforced by Sentry. Dynamic detection requires sufficient history and Seer availability.
Creation can fail after persisting a monitor, especially during Dynamic setup. After an error or timeout, use find_metric_monitors with the name and project before retrying; do not assume rollback or blindly repeat creation.

name: create_monitor
title: Create Cron Monitor
description:
Create a Sentry cron monitor.

Use this tool when you need to:
- Monitor a scheduled job (cron job, scheduled task) for missed, failed, or slow runs
- Set up a cron monitor before instrumenting check-ins

Set `schedule` to exactly one crontab or interval schedule. Check-ins must still be sent by the job (SDK `monitor_config`/check-ins or `sentry monitor run`) using the returned slug.
workflowIds optionally connect existing notification Alerts without modifying them. Use find_alert_rules(kind='issue') to find workflow IDs.
If the returned status is `disabled` but you did not request that, the organization has no cron monitor seat available. Tell the user; the monitor ignores check-ins until a seat frees up and it is enabled.
After an error or timeout, use find_monitors with the name and project before retrying; creation is not idempotent.

<examples>
create_monitor(organizationSlug='my-organization', projectSlug='backend', name='Nightly Import', schedule={ type: 'crontab', crontab: '0 3 * * *' }, timezone='America/Los_Angeles', checkInMargin=5, maxRuntime=30)
create_monitor(organizationSlug='my-organization', projectSlug='backend', name='Queue Drain', schedule={ type: 'interval', value: 15, unit: 'minute' })
</examples>

name: find_dropped_events
title: Find Dropped Events
description:
Find events dropped before they were stored in Sentry — ground-truth data-fidelity information about what was and wasn't captured.

Events can be dropped client-side in the SDK (sample_rate, before_send) or
server-side at ingest (rate limited, over quota, filtered, invalid, abuse/spike
protection, cardinality limited). Accepted-only views (searches, aggregates,
charts) can't show this, so the data may be incomplete in ways they don't reveal
— for example, a flat or spiky chart caused entirely by drops.

Use this tool when you need to:

name: get_profile
title: Get Transaction Profile
description:
Analyze aggregated CPU profiling data (flamegraph) for a transaction to identify performance bottlenecks and detect regressions.
For one specific profile by ID or URL, use get_profile_details.

USE THIS TOOL WHEN:
- User asks why a specific endpoint/transaction is slow
- User wants to understand where CPU time is spent
- User asks about performance bottlenecks
- User wants to compare performance between time periods
- User shares a Sentry profile URL

RETURNS:
- Hot paths (call stacks consuming the most CPU time); the last frame of each stack is the primary bottleneck
- Performance percentiles (p75, p95, p99) for each function
- User code vs library code breakdown
- Regression analysis when comparing periods

<examples>
### Analyze from URL (with transaction name)
```
get_profile(
  profileUrl='https://my-org.sentry.io/explore/profiling/profile/backend/flamegraph/?profilerId=abc123',
  transactionName='/api/users'
)
```

### Analyze by transaction name
```
get_profile(
  organizationSlug='my-org',
  transactionName='/api/users',
  projectSlugOrId='backend'
)
```

### Compare performance between periods
```
get_profile(
  organizationSlug='my-org',
  transactionName='/api/users',
  projectSlugOrId='backend',
  period='7d',
  compareAgainstPeriod='14d'
)
```
</examples>

<hints>
- Use `focusOnUserCode: true` (default) to filter out library code
- High p99 relative to p75 indicates inconsistent performance
- Use compareAgainstPeriod to detect regressions over time
- Transaction names are case-sensitive
- Start optimizing at the bottleneck of the top hot path; look for caching opportunities and N+1 or inefficient data access
- For a major regression, investigate recent changes to that function
- Without profile data, verify the exact transaction name with search_traces, try a longer period (e.g. '30d'), or check that profiling is enabled for the project. If only one comparison period has data, adjust that period or drop compareAgainstPeriod
</hints>
